# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.28 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.27. Written and tested by the author's assistant on one Linux machine; **nothing was tried on Windows, macOS or arm64**.

**New and fixed — phone photos of a book** (tried on a batch of 113 raw phone photos, 222 pages)
- **`--trim-background`** (profile key `trim_background`, checkbox in the settings, in "All options"): after the page is levelled, the table or bag still showing in its corners is painted over. The paper is found as the smooth, bright, colourless surface; its outline keeps the content box, the layout analysis and the OCR off the background.
- **`--fingers` no longer wipes print**: a candidate must be smaller than an eighth of the picture and hold no text between the first and last skin pixel of its rows; warm shadowed paper with text lines was being wiped before.
- **OCR retry**: a page with a large body of content that read (almost) empty is read again on its content box; kept only when it finds clearly more words. On the sample batch it recovered the pages that read 0 words (166, 325 and 280 words).
- **Profiles**: `phone-photos` now also straightens the perspective, wipes the background and cuts open books in the middle; new **`phone-photos-a4`** puts every page on an A4 sheet with the text scaled up to fill it.

**Result on the 113-photo batch**: 222 pages, all 2481×3508 px; 47 617 recognised words; 18 pages with 3 words or fewer (was 26), the rest blank pages, chapter openers or contents pages.

**Verified**: unit tests for the new cleanup, the retry and the setting; the sample batch looked at page by page on contact sheets.
**Not verified**: Windows, macOS, arm64; a head-to-head comparison with ScanTailor on the same photos; the new checkbox's machine-written translations.

**Known limits**: photos that are not pages (a desk, a duplicated cover) are kept; a large hand holding the page can stay; small notches remain where a finger was removed; a folded page corner can be cut diagonally; tables and contents pages with dot leaders read few words. Also unchanged: OCR can misread characters such as `@`; a borderless table is found as two tables; the rotation behaviour seen on Windows 11 is unconfirmed.
